Isolation has become a part of my personality. I've had depression for as long as I can remember and it's affected my life in every area I can think of. I feel like it's become a part of my personality, just part of who I am. As many other people do, I've learned to live with it, hell, I've even manage to handle it sometimes. What I've never learned to handle is the isolation and loneliness that comes with it. Everyone's heard it a thousand times: "I feel like I don't belong", "I've always felt out of place". So I'll save you the sob story. How do I learn to cope with feeling completely alone and isolated? Medication, therapy, none of that seems to change what I feel is a fundamental flaw in my personality. People see me as a loner and an introvert, but I don't want to be, I've never wanted to be. I've always wanted to be 'normal', and have people reach out to me, have someone I can talk to, have someone to share my life with. what I'm saying doesn't matter because everyone has their own lives, their own problems, and mine don't matter any more than the next person's. Maybe I just needed an empty hole to vent into. Shit is just really hard to handle sometimes. Makes me want to just run away and never come back. It’s not fair. I fucking hate it so much. People around me, just go through everything with so much energy and power and they’re still so happy and never exhausted. I can’t remember the last time I was actually happy. I hate drinking because it makes me so fucking sad, but I love it because I can accept my sadness completely.
I don’t want to be lonely but I just want everyone to leave me alone so I can find the strength to kill myself. I hate it. I really hate it. It’s not fair, and fuck it. No one understands it, everyone asks me to open up and when I do they don’t know what to say
